## This run specifically

Fix two GitHub issues in the UsageFoundry repository (Xapicc/UsageFoundry). Both are the same shape — a client page that lies to the operator when a request fails — but they are in different files and do not interact. Do them in this order and commit them as two separate commits. Read each issue body in full with `gh issue view <n>` before starting on it.

=== Issue #54 (do this one first, it is the smaller) — https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/54 ===
"Chat Stop leaves every button disabled when its request rejects", severity high. `stop` in `src/app/chat/page.tsx` (~306-318) sets the page-wide `busy` flag and then awaits a bare `fetch` with no `try`. If that fetch rejects (server restarted, connection dropped, browser offline) the rejection propagates out of the handler and the trailing `setBusy(false)` never runs. `busy` disables the composer, Send, Stop, Select all, Reject and Approve, all three of its writers refuse to run while it is set, and nothing shows an error — the only way back is a reload. This is #26 all over again, which was fixed for `send`; `stop` was added later for #22 and did not get the same treatment. `send` and `decide` both go through `chatRequest` inside try/finally.
Fix: move `stop` onto `chatRequest` (or a try/finally), so `busy` is released however the request ended and a failure puts a sentence in `sendError` exactly as a failed Send does.
Regression test: drive the handler's shape with a rejecting fetch and assert the flag is cleared. `src/lib/jsonRequest.test.ts` and `src/lib/chatRequest.test.ts` are the precedent — if `stop` moves onto `chatRequest`, that helper's own guarantee is what you can assert against.
Out of scope: do not change `send` or `decide`; do not change `/api/chat/[id]/cancel`; do not split `busy` into per-button flags — the shared flag is deliberate (one billed child per conversation) and the fix is releasing it, not narrowing it.

=== Issue #56 — https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/56 ===
"Workflow page calls every template deleted when the list fails to load", severity medium. `src/app/workflows/[id]/page.tsx` reads the template list in its own effect (~91-98) with an empty `.catch`, and `guardLabel` (~127-136) has only two states, so `templates === []` — the initial value, and the permanent value when the request fails or answers a non-2xx JSON body — renders every templated block as a red `template deleted` badge. That is the one thing on the page that says the workflow will not run, and it is untrue: Run works normally. It also flashes on every cold load between the two responses.
Fix: three states, not two — not yet read, read and present, read and absent. Until the list has been read a block's guards are unknown and the badge must not claim deletion; a failed read should say the guards could not be checked, in the same shape as `pollError` on that page. Note a non-2xx does not reach the `.catch` at all (`r.json()` resolves for a 401 or a 500 with a body), so check `res.ok` as well.
Acceptance: with `/api/templates` failing no block claims its template was deleted and the page says the guards could not be read; with the route answering, a block naming a genuinely deleted template still shows the danger badge; between the two responses on a cold load no danger badge renders. Regression test over the three-state decision — extract it into a pure helper in `src/lib` so `npm test` can reach it (it compiles `src/lib/**` plus `*.test.tsx`).
Out of scope, and important: do NOT change `src/components/WorkflowEditor.tsx` (it makes the same test but already gates on `loaded` and reports the failure; adopting any shared helper there is a separate change). Do NOT remove the deleted-template call-out itself — `planNode` refuses a node whose template has been deleted by name, and this page is where an operator sees that before pressing Run. Do not make the templates read gate the whole page behind the skeleton.

=== Both ===
Done looks like: `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both pass (run them; report the real output), both fixes committed to your own branch as separate commits, and BOTH issues closed on GitHub with their own comment saying what you changed, which files, how you tested it, and naming your branch (`git branch --show-current`) since the fixes are not landed yet: `gh issue close 54 --comment "…"` and `gh issue close 56 --comment "…"`.

Practical notes: you are working in an isolated git worktree, so `node_modules` may be absent — run `npm install` first if it is. Do not push, do not open a pull request; the operator lands the branch. Do not edit CLAUDE.md or README.md: several runs are working this repository in parallel and those two files are shared conflict surface, and neither fix changes a documented invariant.

If — and only if — one of these cannot be resolved without a decision only a human can make, then as an absolute last resort: finish the other one normally, leave the blocked one's files untouched, post a comment on the blocked issue explaining exactly what decision is needed and why you stopped, and do NOT close that one. Only if BOTH are blocked: make no changes at all, run `git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd` so your branch carries no commits and the tree is clean, comment on both issues, and finish. Both issues spell out a fix direction, so prefer the smallest change that satisfies each.
